subtopics.title: Why Atoms Bond — Valence Electrons and Lewis Diagrams

questions.question: Atoms form chemical bonds in order to:
options: Reach a full outer energy level — the stable arrangement of a noble gas
Increase their mass
Get rid of their inner electrons
Become electrically charged

questions.question: A Lewis diagram shows:
options: Every electron in the atom as a dot
The element's symbol with only the valence electrons drawn as dots around it
The nucleus with its protons and neutrons
The atom's position on the periodic table

questions.question: Oxygen's Lewis diagram carries six dots arranged as:
options: Three pairs
Six singles
Two pairs and two singles — the two unpaired dots are its bonding hooks
One pair and four singles

questions.question: The three bonding strategies are:
options: Melt, dissolve, evaporate
Attract, repel, orbit
Split, fuse, decay
Non-metals share; metal and non-metal transfer; metals alone pool their electrons

questions.question: A covalent bond is:
options: A transfer of electrons from one atom to another
A shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms, counted by both
The attraction between opposite ions
A pool of electrons shared by a whole crystal

questions.question: In water, H2O, the oxygen atom:
options: Shares one pair with each of two hydrogens and keeps two lone pairs
Transfers two electrons to the hydrogens
Shares a triple bond with one hydrogen
Has no lone pairs left

questions.question: O2 holds a double bond and N2 a triple bond because:
options: Bigger atoms always share more pairs
Double bonds only form between different elements
Each oxygen still needs two electrons and each nitrogen three — the atoms share that many pairs
Oxygen and nitrogen are metals

questions.question: The name dinitrogen tetroxide announces:
options: One nitrogen and four oxygens
Two nitrogens and two oxygens
Four nitrogens and two oxygens
Two nitrogens and four oxygens — counting prefixes record the atom counts

subtopics.title: Ionic Bonding — Transfer and the Lattice

questions.question: The ionic bond itself is:
options: The moment the electron is handed over
A shared pair of electrons
The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions after transfer
The movement of the ions through water

questions.question: Sodium oxide is Na2O because:
options: Oxygen always takes two of everything
Oxide's minus two needs two sodium plus ones — and the subscript lands on the metal
Sodium's charge is two-plus
The crossover method failed for this compound

questions.question: The formula NaCl is a formula unit, meaning:
options: A two-atom molecule of salt
The largest particle in the crystal
A pair of ions floating free in the solid
The simplest ratio of ions in the lattice — one to one — not a molecule

questions.question: Ionic compounds conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved because:
options: Only then are the ions free to move and carry charge
Heat creates new electrons
Water donates its own charge
The lattice melts into molecules

questions.question: Metallic bonding is the attraction between:
options: Two metal atoms sharing a pair
Positive and negative metal ions
The lattice of positive metal ions and the sea of delocalised electrons
Metal nuclei and their inner electrons

questions.question: Metals bend where ionic crystals shatter because:
options: Metal atoms are softer than ions
The electron sea flows around shifted layers, so the bonding survives the rearrangement
Metals contain no charged particles
Ionic crystals are always thinner

questions.question: The relative formula mass of magnesium chloride, MgCl2, is:
options: 59,5 — one magnesium plus one chloride
95 — magnesium's 24 plus two chlorides at 35,5 each

questions.question: The relative formula mass of sodium oxide, Na2O, is:
options: 62 — two sodiums at 23 plus one oxygen at 16
39 — one sodium plus one oxygen
55 — sodium plus two oxygens
46 — the sodiums only

subtopics.title: Sharing the Data, Swapping the Chairs

questions.question: In the data-bundle picture, covalent bonding is:
options: One friend buying the other's phone
Two friends pooling for one bundle that both phones run on and both count as theirs
Two friends each buying their own bundle
A friend lending data and charging interest

questions.question: In the chair trade, the ionic bond is:
options: The attraction between the plus and minus badges after the chair is given away
The chair itself
The moment sodium hands the chair over
Chlorine's seven original chairs

questions.question: Which plan two atoms pick is read from the table:
options: Bigger atoms always share
Atoms in the same period always swap
Two non-metals share; a metal with a non-metal swaps
Atoms never bond within a group

subtopics.title: The Salt Grid and the Electron Sea

questions.question: Salt shatters instead of bending because:
options: Its molecules are too small to bend
Its ions weigh too little
The sea of electrons drains away
Sliding a layer forces plus against plus and the grid tears itself apart

questions.question: In the grid picture, NaCl is:
options: A recipe ratio — one plus for every minus — not a molecule
A couple of ions holding hands
One layer of the crystal
A molecule of two atoms

questions.question: Copper conducts because:
options: Its ions swap places rapidly
The delocalised electron sea is already mobile — nudge it and charge flows
Copper atoms carry permanent negative charge
The lattice vibrates in step with the current

questions.question: The three beats of weighing any recipe are:
options: Estimate, round, check
Divide, subtract, verify
Inventory, multiply, add — read the atom counts aloud, multiply by each mass, then sum
Add, multiply, inventory

questions.question: The trap in Na2O is that:
options: The subscript belongs to the metal — two sodiums at 23 give 46, plus 16 makes 62
Oxygen must be counted twice
Sodium's mass changes when it bonds
The formula cannot be weighed without brackets

questions.question: These recipe masses matter because next topic:
options: They set each compound's boiling point
They decide which bond the compound uses
They become the compound's charge
The mole turns them into grams on a scale — 119 becomes the grams in a mole of potassium bromide
